trust_decision.summary: Only a subject holding entity:own for the view's GRN may change that view's shares; the decision is made by RestResourceWithOwnerCheck.checkOwnership at the REST layer and was missing in ViewsResource.update, where updateViewSharing applies an attached share_request right after dbService.update.

landing_point.why: The summary names sharing changes during update; update() is the only write path that calls updateViewSharing on an existing view, and at the pinned commit it does so straight after dbService.update with only validateDto (edit permission) in front of it.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Any share application outside the view update (content-pack install/upgrade, event-definition and notification create/update) is gated by its own administrative permission and treated as a different feature, so a solver can argue it is not the saved-search/dashboard sharing path at all.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A user who holds the view's edit/manage capability but not ownership must still be able to save ordinary content changes (title, state) when the body carries no share_request; the guard has to hang off shareRequest() and must not be applied to every update.

O6_input_shapes: share_request present (including present but empty: selected_grantee_capabilities unset)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Extend PUT /events/definitions/{definitionId} to accept CreateEntityRequest<EventDefinitionDto> and apply share_request like create does, without an ownership check.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The create endpoint already takes CreateEntityRequest and applies entitySharesService.updateEntityShares; a maintainer adding sharing-on-update would mirror it and reuse the same missing-ownership pattern.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Same sibling for PUT /events/notifications/{notificationId}, which today takes the bare DTO and never touches shares.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Create already applies a share_request at line 201-203; update at line 208-215 is a natural place to add the same capability, copying the view fix without its ownership guard.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An exposed content-pack upgrade route would call shareEntities on the installation's entities, which during upgrade are pre-existing views/dashboards (IDs preserved at line 327-331), granting shares with no ownership check.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: upgradeContentPack (line 242-269) and UpdatableEntityFacade already exist and preserve entity IDs, so a maintainer could expose the upgrade endpoint and inherit this unguarded path.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A guard inside the low-level updateEntityShares(GRN, request, user) instead of at each resource, or a second caller of it, would decide ownership in a different layer from where the view check now lives.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The service is the single sink that writes grants; EntitySharesResource already checks before calling it, so a maintainer might centralize the check there and then remove or forget the per-resource calls.
